name: Kyoto
dek: JMA's 1991–2020 normal for Kyoto. The station is not in the NOAA file that the Tokyo sheet uses.
paragraphs: Japan's NOAA submission has Tokyo and Osaka and does not have Kyoto. The table is the Japan Meteorological Agency's monthly normal for Kyoto, precinct 61, block 47759, period 1991–2020, with 30 years in each temperature and precipitation column. The position and the height, 40.81 m, are the OSCAR record for WIGOS 0-20000-0-47759. The JMA page does not print them.

The average high runs from a cool January to a hotter August than Tokyo's, and July is the heaviest precipitation month in this table. None of those figures is blended with Osaka or with Tokyo. The plug, the road rule, and the tipping note are the national ones.

climate.caption: Station: Kyoto, JMA block 47759. Not in the NOAA NCEI Japan submission.
climate.note: Monthly high, low, and precipitation are the 1991–2020 normals on the Japan Meteorological Agency page for Kyoto (precinct 61, block 47759), each with 30 years of data. Kyoto has no file in the NOAA NCEI Japan submission, version 6.6. Position and height are the OSCAR/Surface record whose WIGOS identifier is 0-20000-0-47759: latitude 35.0147222222, longitude 135.7327777778, elevation 40.81 m (https://oscar.wmo.int/surface/rest/api/search/station?wmoIndex=47759). The JMA normals page does not print those three figures, and they were not taken from it.

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type A and B, 100 V, 50 and 60 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list shows Japan at 100 volts, with 50 hertz and 60 hertz, and plug types A and B. The country line does not say which frequency belongs to which city, so this sheet does not pick one. The same line is in the copy of that page archived on 16 August 2026.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: The Japanese Law Translation database's English text of the Road Traffic Act says, in Article 17(4), that a vehicle must proceed along the part of the road to the left of the center. Article 18(1) says a motor vehicle that is not on a road with vehicle traffic lanes must proceed down the left side of the road, except when passing, when moving toward the center or the right edge under other articles, or when road conditions compel it.
driving.sourceTitle: Road Traffic Act, Articles 17 and 18, Japanese Law Translation

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.detail: The Japan National Tourism Organization says it is not common to tip for bars, cafes, restaurants, taxis, and hotels. It describes a separate custom, kokorozuke, and says a private guide or interpreter who is used to overseas practice may accept a tip, which is not expected and, if offered, is put in an envelope.

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Japan, last reviewed 25 August 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Yen and the code JPY for Japan.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone1970.tab lists Japan on Asia/Tokyo, and Japan has only that one row. The comment on the row names Eyre Bird Observatory. The file's header says a comment is useful only for a country that has more than one zone. The comment is not a description of Japan, and it is not printed as one.
